how_it_was_unblocked: cmake's find_package(Torch) pulls in Caffe2Config.cmake, which refuses to configure when CUDA is absent — the installed wheel is a CUDA build (2.13.0+cu130) and there is no GPU here. But that wheel still ships libtorch_cpu.so and c10, so the fix is to skip cmake's Torch package entirely and link the CPU libraries directly: g++ -I<torch>/include -I<torch>/include/torch/csrc/api/include -L<torch>/lib -ltorch_cpu -lc10, with _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1 to match the wheel. The blocker was cmake's CUDA insistence, not a missing library.
model_export: OpenDriveFM traced to TorchScript from a real keyframe through a thin (x, velocity) wrapper with ego_deltas baked in as a buffer, then frozen. 60 MB module, plus a 4 MB reference bundle carrying the input tensors and the Python reference outputs.

parity.determinism: PASS — identical outputs on a repeated forward
parity.note: Re-measured against the module re-exported with the MHA fastpath disabled and the calibrated trust checkpoint. Trust is still bit-identical; occupancy differs at float32 rounding.

runner.what: Two threads: a producer at a fixed sensor rate, a consumer running inference. Measures queue wait, inference, and END-TO-END staleness — how old the frame behind the current occupancy grid is.
runner.finding: This is the whole argument for the seqlock. Inference latency is the SAME under both policies (178 vs 183 ms p50) — but end-to-end staleness is 235 ms with latest-frame and 2,319 ms with FIFO, a 10x difference the model latency number cannot show. A system honestly reporting '180 ms inference' was handing the planner 2.3-second-old perception.

primitives.flakiness: test_spsc_ring failed once during a -j4 parallel build, then passed 40/40 alone — CPU contention in a timing-sensitive test, the kind CI hides.

hardware: cloud container CPU, 4 cores, g++ -O2, no -march=native, 2 torch threads. No GPU.
caveats: Every latency figure is CPU. No CUDA, no TensorRT, no GPU was benchmarked; the deadline-miss rates are what a CPU-only build gives and are not a claim about deployable hardware.

ego_deltas is baked into the traced module from one keyframe. The runner measures latency and staleness, where that does not matter, and the parity check compares against Python run with the same baked value.
The 33.3 ms budget in the parity output is a 30 Hz reference, not a target this build meets.

integrity_monitor.hardware: two platforms: Linux VM (aarch64, Apple Silicon) and cloud container (x86-64), g++ -O3, single thread, no -march=native
integrity_monitor.reference: scripts/odfm_geom.py (camera_ground_coverage, integrity_map) and scripts/odfm_ground.py (visibility_from), on nuScenes scene-0061

parity.note: Bit-identical on aarch64. On x86-64 the same source differs by 1.9e-09, which is float32 accumulation order, not an algorithmic difference — float32 storage of a value in [0,1] already carries ~6e-08.

integrity_monitor.test: cpp/tests/test_integrity_monitor.cpp, registered with ctest; skips with a message rather than passing vacuously when the dumped case is absent
integrity_monitor.why: This is the one piece the traced model does not provide. The TorchScript graph gives occupancy, trajectory and trust; the observability map is computed from calibration and an occupancy grid, in Python, at 216x216 for six cameras. A deployed runner cannot call back into Python for it, so it had to exist in C++ — and once it does, the whole monitor runs in 10.9 ms, inside the 33.3 ms budget the 296 ms model misses by an order of magnitude.
stages: Projected AREA of each cell quad in the image, by shoelace on the four projected corners, normalised by 140 px and clipped to 1. Not a binary frustum test: a cell at 54 m is viewed at grazing incidence and images to a sliver, and must not count as evidence equal to a cell at 5 m.

Bearing-bucket cast from the CAMERA position, not the LiDAR — the cameras sit up to 1.7 m forward and 1 m to the side, so casting from the sensor origin puts every shadow in the wrong place. A running minimum over three neighbouring bearings closes the sliver gap a one-cell obstacle would leave.
integrity = 1 − ∏(1 − trust · coverage · visible). Independence is an upper bound, not an unbiased estimate: six cameras on one vehicle share weather, sun and a power rail.
caveats: CPU only. No CUDA path exists in either environment to compare against.
The port is validated against one real keyframe, not the full 404 — parity at 1.9e-09 on 216²×6 grids is what the check is for, not coverage of the dataset.

provenance_note: The exporter's --frames default was 1, which silently produces a DIFFERENT model: v11_temporal consumes a four-frame window, and every ADE number on this console was measured with four. A one-frame export traces a quarter of the work and benchmarks at 67 ms against this 200 ms — a 3x 'speedup' that is really a change of model. The default is now 4 and the traced shape is recorded here so the two can never be compared by accident.
